name: Bazil Thredd
summary: In Stormwind, Bazil Thredd holds insight into the Defias Brotherhood's lingering plots. After an unsent letter is recovered from the Deadmines, City Architect Baros Alexston directs you to the Defias leader's right-hand man, now locked beneath the streets in the high-security Stockade.

sections.title: A Bitter History
sections.body: Baros Alexston shares a bitter history with Edwin VanCleef. Both led the Stonemasons Guild, charged with rebuilding Stormwind from the ashes of the First and Second Wars. When the kingdom's magnificent white walls and towers were finished, the nobility refused to pay the masons their promised wages. Some senior members received bureaucratic posts to quiet them, but VanCleef refused to abandon the rank-and-file laborers. He led a violent riot out of the city and founded the Defias Brotherhood.

sections.title: A Turn to the Stockade
sections.body: To learn VanCleef's full design and what the Brotherhood still plans against Stormwind, Alexston directs you to Bazil Thredd. Thredd was VanCleef's chief lieutenant during the mason uprising. He was captured and confined in the city's prison beneath the canals of the Mage Quarter. At the gates, Warden Thelwater warns that the inmates have rebelled, and the Stockade has become a warzone.

faq.answer: Bazil Thredd was Edwin VanCleef's primary lieutenant in the Stonemasons Guild and the early Defias uprising. Stormwind authorities captured him and imprisoned him deep within the Stockade.

faq.q: Why does Baros Alexston send you to speak with Thredd?
faq.answer: After examining the unsent letter from the Deadmines, Alexston sees that Stormwind faces a threat beyond the Deadmines. As VanCleef's former right-hand man, Thredd understands the Brotherhood's inner workings and remaining schemes better than anyone else, Alexston believes.

faq.q: Why was the Stonemasons Guild betrayed?
faq.answer: After the masons rebuilt Stormwind following the Second War, the House of Nobles refused to honor its financial agreements. The laborers were left unpaid and destitute. VanCleef rejected quiet bribes to silence him and led a riot out of the city gates.
The Stockade entrance lies along the canals in Stormwind's northeastern Mage Quarter. Warden Thelwater stands just inside, trying to hold back escaping prisoners.

faq.q: What is happening inside the Stockade when you arrive?
faq.answer: When you arrive, Bazil Thredd and the other inmates have overpowered the guards, unlocked the holding cells, and seized the lower halls. Warden Thelwater struggles to keep the riot from spilling into Stormwind's streets.

faq.q: How did Baros Alexston avoid joining the Defias?
faq.answer: VanCleef refused compromise and chose armed rebellion, while Alexston was among the senior guild craftsmen who accepted government employment from the kingdom. He eventually became City Architect.

angles.text: As a human, you see the Stonemasons Guild's rebellion laid bare the deep political fracture between Stormwind's ruling nobility and the commoners who built the city with their own hands.
As an Alliance hero, you face a Defias threat reaching into the capital through the unsecured cells of the Stockade, even with Edwin VanCleef slain.
As a rogue, you know Thredd represents the hardened, organized underworld branch of the Defias, who traded construction hammers for shanks and street violence.
